key_insight: Large-scale DMRG provides a high-accuracy classical benchmark for the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, and current NISQ methods fall behind except at very small problem sizes.
engineering_relevance: The study helps quantum engineers assess when tensor-network classical solvers still outperform noisy quantum algorithms and where hybrid subspace methods may be more practical.
method: DMRG on NERSC Perlmutter to compute LMG ground-state energies up to 1400 particles
Compare classical benchmark results against VQE and SQD on an IBM Eagle quantum computer
Use ground-state energy error as the main performance metric
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a large LMG dataset with accurate energies up to 1400 particles, with VQE staying within 1% error only for 6 particles and SQD extending this to 17 particles.
watch_item: Results are tied to a specific noisy hardware setup and problem instance, so conclusions may not generalize directly to other quantum devices or model parameters.
paper_title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulations of the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick Model Using Large Tensor Networks
